ActionRevisiting the “Reconsideration of the National Ambient Air Quality Standards for Particulate Matter” (89 FR 16202; March 6, 2024).
Reasons for ActionConcerns that the regulation may not be squarely grounded in statutory authority.The previous Administration reconsidered the 2020 PM NAAQS and EPA is evaluating the appropriateness of that reconsideration.Align the standard-setting process with statutory requirements and alleviate unnecessary burdens.
Important facts on regulation/programCost estimated at $7 billion over the next 20 years (at least $470 million a year).Costs could be even higher, because the illustrative cost estimate doesn’t fully account for all the controls and emissions reductions needed to meet the standard in some places.Concerns have also been raised related to:Burdens states with planning requirements.Hinders American manufacturing with burdensome Clean Air Act permitting requirements that deter economic growth.
Groups or entities requesting reconsiderationStatesCompaniesTrade associations
